Edit: Wow this review got a lot more publicity than I expected! That being said, now that I've played a bit more I'd like to revise my initial thoughts. Battlefield V has the hallmarks of a good game, the bullet ballistics are good, team work and strategy is good, the graphics and cool WW2 weaponry are good. But all this is over-arched by critical flaws that I'm guessing were the result of EA deciding this game wasn't likely to be as profitable as they were expecting. Customization feels lacking at best with a lot of cosmetic items being really boring or really expensive to encourage the use of in game currency. Weapon customization has similar problems with only a few "specializations" for each weapon, mostly making it magically have less recoil or reload faster among other uncreative things. The most critical flaw this game suffers is the complete abandonment by the developers. They obviously knew their time wouldn't make them money and decided to leave the game in a state that feels late beta at best. There's a lot of controversy in the comments about me saying the game is plagued by hackers but I stand by this statement. It's been abandoned, players don't get banned, reports don't get answered. If you want to play the game despite these flaws because you like WW2 or the Battlefield series, there's definetly fun to be had but heres a few tips:

* Avoid official servers: that's right, the official servers receive seemingly 0 maintenance and manually administrated servers are massively more effective at banning hackers than the official servers. EA you should be ashamed.
* Consider avoiding if you live in a remote area: In Australia today I was able to find just 1 conquest server with 40 players and able to at least play the game (10AM on a Wednesday). I really can't guarantee that there will be any player base if you live somewhere more exotic than Australia, USA and Europe are probably okay. Don't count on being able to find a server if you're a night owl like me.

Overall this game had a lot of potential but it stands as a hollow shell of what it could have been. I liked the inclusion of female characters and being able to play as someone who I felt more of a connection to but the amount of hostility EA showed towards their player base was uncalled for and instead of making up for it they took the money and ran.

A bitter failure, partly down to dreadful communication and a glaring lack of effort on the part of the developers, Battlefield V is now almost three years old – so what has changed?

- First and foremost, I should point out that I’ve been playing Battlefield V since its release, across various platforms. So I reckon I’ve seen quite a few changes over the past three years, but I don’t intend to cover them all.-

Graphically, it’s a real treat. Honestly, we wouldn’t have expected anything less, but the game looks stunning even with the graphics set to minimum; there’s been some real work put into the lighting, environments and facial models.
Truly, the game is pure eye candy and will delight screenshot enthusiasts.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2461174029

The single-player story is quite similar to that of *Battlefield 1*, in that it takes us through four different war stories. The aim here was to explore and recount events that are little-known or rarely depicted in various media.

And, er… Well, first of all, it’s interesting from a narrative perspective: the Norwegian resistance in Narvik, the crew of a Tiger tank in Berlin, the Senegalese troops in Provence, the rowdy team of future SAS and SBS members; in short, you get the picture – it’s quite enticing and piques your curiosity.

Each story (as well as the intro and outro) is brought to life by some pretty wild narration, accompanied by music by Johan Söderqvist and Patrik Andrén, as well as numerous explanatory messages; everything is actually very, very well written. It’s lovely, it’s interesting, it’s short, it’s a bit educational, and it’s fun. You might find the length of the solo campaign a bit of a let-down, and perhaps the stories a bit lacklustre if you take them out of their historical context, but in itself it’s a massive plus for a change from the US-centric stories we’ve seen in Call of Duty: World War II, for example.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2483811958

Apart from that, there’s the ever-present multiplayer mode – the one that’s been the subject of so much discussion.
I’m certainly not going to dwell on customisation again. It’s there; there are loads of skins, many of which are rather odd – let’s move on.

Ultimately, Battlefield hasn’t really changed since BF1. The concept remains the same, the game modes are similar, but the gameplay itself is… different.

Admittedly, the TTK keeps fluctuating wildly and DICE clearly still haven’t managed to sort it out, but it seems that after three years, people have got used to this version of BFV. Lying down, crouching, running whilst crouched, etc.—Battlefield V has, despite everything, managed to adapt its own mechanics and change its gameplay to make the whole thing feel more… realistic and to expand the possibilities.

Because yes, you can now run for cover to dodge bullets, build your own defences with sandbags at strategic points, use your squad points to call for help, a vehicle, or even a barrage on an enemy position. You can revive your teammates, heal yourself, and loot corpses to find ammunition. Whilst it isn’t a simulation, I think this BFV is the instalment that best blurs the line between arcade and simulation.

But ultimately, where the multiplayer is most intense is in its attention to detail and the experience it delivers. I’ve already mentioned the game’s beauty, but every detail has benefited from a huge amount of work, both in terms of research and execution. In the heat of the moment, you don’t realise it – you’re just playing. But when you take a step back, you find yourself experiencing something quite intense. Sneaking through the jungle of the Solomon Islands, jumping at the slightest sound of footsteps; fleeing at the sound of the sirens from the Stukas as they dive; looking up in a futile attempt to locate the source of the rumble from the V1 rocket that might – just might – come crashing down on you; hearing your crew coughing inside your tank after it’s been through some gruelling battles – and so on.

It’s a completely mad experience, and even after three years of playing, I still find myself discovering new details like this. That’s really what makes BFV so great.

[h1] A concise review of Battlefield V after around 400+ hours of gameplay.[/h1]
[b]PROS:[/b]
+ Outstanding Visuals.
+ Phenomenal Gunplay.
+ Great Soundtrack.
+ More In-depth Movement system that offers a wealth of traversal options compared to other 
    Battlefield titles 
+ Well thought out gameplay mechanics that complement each other.
+ More focused on Squad play compared to other battlefields.
+ Decent amount of content.
+ A wealthy amount of Character cosmetics for you to grind for.

[b]CONS:[/b]
- Not nearly as immersive as Battlefield 1 due to questionable character cosmetic choices.
- Lots and Lots of cheaters. Depending on what servers you play on, the amount may vary. [b]Note: Cheaters seem really prominent on Asia in official servers, US and EU are a lot 
  more bearable but you'll have the most luck finding clean matches on Custom Servers.[/b]
- Shorter Live-service lifespan. DICE cut support on the game as it was getting good, so any 
 remaining bugs will not get fixed and there's not going to be any new content.

Overall, Battlefield V sets itself apart from others with its more hardcore and team play focused nature. It offers superb gunplay, a strong gameplay foundation, outstanding visuals, and a decent amount of existing content. Though a lot of it's short comings are apparent due to issues with cheaters and the lack of support.
I'd give this an 8.5/10 based how much better it's gotten and the fact on what it could have been. 

If you're thinking of getting it, I'd highly recommend getting it on sale.

Battlefield V is a rollercoaster of emotions, pure chaos wrapped in stunning visuals and heart-pounding action. After a long, grueling day at work, there’s nothing better than jumping into the fray with your colleague by your side. The rush of storming objectives, laying down suppressive fire, or barely surviving a tank assault together creates a bond like no other. It’s the kind of fun that makes you forget the grind of the day and lose yourself in the madness of war.

But then, the cheaters show up. Nothing kills the vibe faster than lining up the perfect shot, only to be insta-killed by someone snapping their aim halfway across the map with inhuman precision. You look at the killcam, and there they are, spinning like a broken lawn sprinkler, headshotting everyone in sight. Rage boils over. You scream at the screen. Where’s the anti-cheat system? How does a game this beautiful, this immersive, get tarnished by such blatant hacks? It’s maddening.

Yet somehow, Battlefield V keeps pulling you back in. The maps are breathtaking—every corner of the game feels alive, from the snow-covered peaks of Narvik to the fiery ruins of Rotterdam. And when you’re with your colleague, even the most frustrating moments become something to laugh about. You’ll rage together when a cheater wipes your squad, but then you’ll crack up after respawning and accidentally crashing your plane straight into each other. The game shines in those moments of shared chaos, where teamwork and laughter triumph over frustration.

The class system makes every match feel like a collaborative effort. One of you drops medkits while the other lays down ammo, and suddenly you’re an unstoppable team. Every kill feels earned, every revive feels like a small victory, and every explosion reminds you why you keep coming back. Sure, cheaters are a plague, but they can’t take away the camaraderie and pure joy of tearing through the battlefield with a friend.

Battlefield V is far from perfect, but when you’re dodging bullets and cracking jokes with your colleague after a hard day, the flaws fade into the background. The cheaters will always be there to annoy you, but the chaos and adrenaline-fueled fun will keep you coming back for more, one epic moment at a time.

One of the most confusing and ill-suited Battlefield titles ever. To anyone who complained about women, people of color and the disabled at launch - you we're complaining about the wrong things. Sure, it ruined the immersion of World War 2 and the 'less seen' battles of that War are displayed instead of the well known ones. These, (well being breaking for some) aren't core aspects that make this game feel like such a shell. These are...  

Multiplayer:

The map design is too wide-spread and objectives feel out of place. You will have trouble finding where to go on most farmland maps: it feels like DICE just dropped a letter down on a random spot and said "HAH! THIS IS B!". There's no significance to B, it's just there. If anyone has played Battlefield 3 or 4 they'd know the significance of objectives and their unlock capabilities, tanks; helicopters, LAVs, etc. Battlefield 1 tarnished this by giving everyone a bomber to mass genocide everyone on objectives; V doesn't even put thought into it at all.

The gun-play feels incredibly artificial. In the former i described how immersion can make or break a game - this is one of the things that broke BFV for me. DICE in their willingness to be all inclusive seemingly dropped a ton of guns onto their new game which they already had assets for in their previous. I understand that not much time had passed since World War 1 and that the B.A.R, Lewis and Selb were still in service but they weren't the 'same' weapons. These weapons literally feel like you're playing Battlefield 1. The sights are terrible and HMGs don't even come with a telescopic, something BF1 even had. I love HMGs. They're so big and sexy. UWU. ...And for some reason i can't stand up and aim. Odd. I could do that in every other Battlefield game...
Devaluing the Support Class was a deal breaker for me.

Passive and/or obvious hackers are everywhere. Within 3.9 hours of gameplay i was in three to four different games all with hackers. You know it's bad when the same amount of people are spectating and watching these people for their own entertainment. 
This game is not worth its pricetag. It is an indie shooter that looks nice. It is not a AAA game.
Refund me please daddy.

Campaign:

Befitting to its theme: the campaign is goofy and brings forth a sense of non-urgentness. All while trying to tell you "this is serious!" and that you should respect the sacrifice these soldiers made. I felt like these missions resembled Battlefield 1 too much: attack the tower; report back, grab the notes, come back, next objective of the same caliber. Really linear stuff. The convict mission (the planes and bombs) was charming yet extraordinarily lacking in substance as if it was some sort of tutorial. I don't play Battlefield for the campaign but they [DICE] just keep getting worse at producing single-player missions which essentially are a portraiture for their game. The Last Tiger by far is the best campaign story mission. 

I don't want to open a can of worms but when you're making a World War 2 game, (especially in a Nazi city which is being blockaded by the allies) you can't honestly tell me at that point that people are hanging up the National German Eagle from World War One. Absolutely breaking immersion because some DICE developer is offended by the swastika. Tumbling down the streets seeing people cry over the dead family as you plow your tank's HMG into incoming American forces and it's the flag that offends you. A flag that we can learn from and an ideology that we can look back on and see as a major mistake never to repeat again. This is the problem with changing history. You could have told us this was an 'alternate timeline' but you didn't. So what exactly are we fighting for? The Last Tiger takes a deep philosophical turn trying not to paint all Nazi soldiers as war criminals or absolute psychopaths while completely removing the purpose of the intent all in one go. This is a special type of stupid.


TL;DR
1) This game hid behind a social justice narrative, a facade of PC culture, to mask its weak production and performance.

2) The game only had half of the time it should have had in production.

3) The developers are ignorant.

4) Game should NOT be sold for full price with all of the unfixed issues.

5) Hackers on every single server: Fairfight is garbage and detects nothing - bring back Punkbuster.

6) Steam unwilling to refund after 2 hours regardless of these issues is a travesty.

Do not buy this game.

This game sends you through the five stages of grief every time you launch it. It's agonizing and the game reeks of wasted potential. The atmosphere is so cool and a good AAA WW2 shooter with all the advancements in modern game developing sounds great on paper and is something I've been craving for a while. As usual with BF titles, there's plenty of fun and neuron stimulating progression, but the way it's handled could be better. And while so many of the design choices and new mechanics are great in theory, they're bogged down by their execution.

For example: The new squad revive system and reworking of medics is good, but the way spawning on squadmates works is mind-boggling. Instead of just being told you can't spawn on a squadmate that's in combat, the game does a series of dramatic GTA pan-ins, pans back out because the spawn isn't safe, then sends you to the map overview so you can't see what your squadmate is doing anymore. You attempt to spawn on them after 15 seconds of delays, oops they were in combat, back to the map overview again. You repeat this process 3 times until you get frustrated and concede to spawning on an objective, which then puts you 200m away from the point and you're forced to jog back to the fight. It's just an unnecessary departure from how spawning worked in the previous games.

However, the greatest offender is the Assignment system. Everyone on the dev team involved with designing this god-forsaken system should not be involved in any future Battlefield games. Battlefield's had some tedious and questionable assignments in the past, but the way they're handled in this game is a new level of terrible user experience. When you hit level 5 and 10 on your weapons, you unlock the Proficiency and Mastery assignments respectively.
These assignments give you the (admittedly very good looking) mint and gold skins for that weapon. This sounds like a fine way to unlock skins for your weapons, but each weapon part is its own assignment (with some exceptions, and the amount you have to do depends on the weapon), so at most you end up doing 7 proficiency and 7 mastery challenges for your weapon. The early assignments range from things like just getting kills or kills while in objective areas with a larger cumulative goal, or a smaller in one round goal if you're gamer enough, and half of these challenges you can do without playing like an idiot or deliberately throwing to get your challenge done. But eventually the cumulative challenges are phased out and it's either in one life or one round, and the challenges themselves start to get asinine.

There's no way these assignments were play-tested by the devs. Kills under 10m with bolt action rifles in 1 life/round, kills over 30m with SMGs that fire marshmallows at that range, 10 headshots while in an objective zone in one life with the semi auto rifles. Most of these later assignments require a perfect storm of a match to pull it off: Your team has to be good enough to secure map control, but not good enough to roll the enemy team because you need the match to last for most of these challenges. You need the enemies to be have no situational awareness and for all the objective ones you have to disadvantage yourself by sitting on the point yourself for some and waiting for your enemies to step on the point for others, instead of just defending/attacking the objective from a better angle off the point.

Okay so the challenges themselves suck balls, great, but you're blazing through the majority of them one round after the other because you're on a hot-streak. Do the challenges automatically roll over into the next one after you complete them? Of fucking course not, and you can't change assignments during the waiting for players phase before the match starts, during the match, or after the match. You have to back out to the main menu, leaving a lobby or squad that you were having fun in, go to the assignment page, equip the next assignment, then if you have a friend in the game, attempt to rejoin the match, and chances are you get put in a queue and miss half of the match. Sometimes multiple people in your group have assignments to progress so you all do a dance alternating people into the lobby so you can keep playing there. And if you start doing your assignments once you hit weapon level 5, the maximum amount of times you'll be doing this dance of dumb is around 14 times (you can alternatively wait until both the proficiencies and masteries are unlocked at the same time and do them together). I've maxed out and completed the assignments for plenty of the weapons, and they're a dampen on the experience every time.

There's no anti-cheat and it's hard to find a match that isn't either riddled with hackers or max-level players sapping all enjoyment out of the game. You get very used to seeing the same names in lobbies and just letting out a groan that it's gonna be one of those matches. Weapon "balancing" is frustrating but that's just par for the course with a DICE game. A lot of the maps are also unenjoyable and poorly balanced.

With all these complaints aside, the visuals and sound design are incredible. DICE and the Frostbite engine always knock it out of the park when it comes to atmosphere. While the gunplay can feel off, the guns themselves look and sound awesome. Firing an MG on a wooden floor and hearing all of the casings rolling on the ground as you fire is so satisfying. Unloading an M1 Garand clip into someone, hearing the satisfying headshot ding followed by the Garand's ping just feels good. Plinking enemies with a suppressed Grease Gun from smoke as they scramble around trying to find you is nice. The game just has an inherent cinematic quality to it, and it's great in that regard. The character voices and voice lines have the usual DICE charm that you can chuckle about if you're not taking it too seriously.

I love the character and weapon customization, and while it's not all historically accurate, the rule of cool is in effect for a lot of it. The bigger issue being that a lot of the cosmetics are overpriced and bundled with things you don't care about to increase their price or are locked behind your standard rotating FOMO shop. Also as someone who got into the game near the end of its life cycle, finding out that a lot of the cool cosmetics were login rewards or in booster packs during the game's past seasons in disheartening, but I guess that's a token Live Service game moment.

There's a large focus on squad-play in this game, and if you have any plans of playing this game, don't go at it alone. Having friends with you as you trudge through the hellscape that is this game makes the experience so much better. In both playing efficiently and dealing with frustation, having the lads there to back you up and laugh off (or share in) the misery makes the game infinitely better.

In summary, the game has some sort of twisted, alluring quality to it. I can't stop playing it, despite how rage-inducing this game is. For some most likely masochistic reason, I keep coming back to it. Even with all my grievances, it's a game that I look forward to hopping on with the lads and playing. And even though it usually sours pretty quickly, that doesn't stop us from playing it for hours. I guess I'd recommend the game, if you're a WW2 fan and need a more arcade style FPS, as it could definitely use the players.

This review is based on 100% completion and 55.5 hours of gameplay.

[h1][b]Recommendation:[/b][/h1]  
Would I recommend this game? I would, but with caveats. While the game is decent, I would encourage players to consider other titles in the [i]Battlefield[/i] series, such as [i]Battlefield 1[/i] and [i]4[/i], before settling on this one. Also, be aware that it's quite large, taking up 91.5GB of space.

Before I go into what I enjoy about this game, I want to highlight an important factor for anyone in the Oceanic region, like myself. Although finding games is possible, you will likely experience a high ping, averaging around 125. Occasionally, you might stumble upon a dedicated Oceanic server, but in my experience, these tended to pop up mainly on weekends. This is crucial to keep in mind since the game is primarily an online experience, and the quality of your connection can significantly impact your enjoyment.

Visually, the game is stunning; the developers have clearly aimed for a cinematic experience in the design. However, the user interface leaves much to be desired. It’s not intuitive at all, and many improvements could have been made to enhance usability. The sound design generally works well, although I found that playing without headphones made everything feel a bit quiet and off. Overall, the audio experience is decent but could be better.

The short campaigns in the game are okay — not remarkable, but they do offer some engaging narratives. I found that when playing on hardcore, the AI can be merciless with their aim, so you'll want to remain close to cover as often as possible. Nevertheless, it is entirely feasible to complete each story on the hardest difficulty.

The multiplayer component, which is the core experience of this game, can be a real mixed bag. It can be exhilarating one moment and incredibly frustrating the next for a variety of reasons. One of the main issues for me is the connectivity. As mentioned earlier, this is largely beyond anyone’s control, but it does create challenges when playing with friends, especially if they live across the globe. In such situations, someone inevitably has to cope with poor connections. Another downside is the presence of cheaters and hackers, which can undoubtedly tarnish the gameplay experience. I encountered two prominent types: one that annihilated the entire lobby repeatedly, including their own team, and another that had speed and invincibility. Additionally, the limited selection of maps can lead to monotony quite quickly. In my case, it was largely due to not enjoying the maps themselves, but this is subjective and may vary for different players. 

For myself, I often found my options limited to conquest modes since those were the only games I could join with a low ping; if you're located closer to Europe or America, this likely won't be an issue for you.

Though I could spend time detailing various complaints about connection issues and the toxic behaviour of some players, I did manage to enjoy myself when the games were running smoothly. There's a broad array of weapons to experiment with across different classes, each offering its own unique playstyle. The vehicles are also quite fun to use [i](I’m referring specifically to tanks, as I struggle with flying in these games)[/i], and like most multiplayer experiences, it's far more enjoyable when played with friends.

In conclusion, the game is a decent choice if you’re looking to hop into a [i]Battlefield[/i] experience. However, if you reside far from major player bases, like I do in the Oceanic region, you might want to think twice before investing your money. While I believe the game has its merits, I would not recommend purchasing it at full price; instead, I suggest waiting for a significant sale before making a decision.
 
[h1][b]Achievements:[/b][/h1]
The achievements in this game are predominantly focused on multiplayer, with a few tied to the campaign and difficulty.

Campaign achievements aren’t too complicated, but they do require you to complete three out of the four stories on the hardest difficulty. This can be quite challenging due to the AI's remarkable aim at this level. I highly recommend taking your time to clear each area before moving on or tackling objectives whenever possible. Stealth is your best friend here; try to engage enemies without drawing too much attention. Fortunately, since you only need to complete three stories, this makes getting the achievements a bit easier.

When it comes to multiplayer achievements, the experience can range from straightforward to quite difficult. Most of the achievements are simple and can be completed during regular gameplay. However, one that I recommend boosting is "Death from Above," which requires you to destroy five manned stationary weapons using an airplane. As someone who struggles to pilot in these games, I found boosting this achievement essential.

To boost effectively, you'll need at least four players [i](two on each side)[/i] to create and/or start a community game. Unfortunately, this game must be set to public, which means random players might join. If this happens, try to communicate your intentions to them and hope they don’t grief you while you’re going for the achievement. One additional issue at the moment is that the game has a bug that prevents you from saving your configurations when setting up a game, so unless you have a previously configured game, you may need to search for a suitable lobby in the browser.

I recommend the map [i]Panzerstorm[/i], as it’s relatively flat, making it easier to achieve the required kills from the air. However, be prepared for a bit of trial and error as it’s still tough to fly.

If you’re looking for more guidance on this achievement, there are excellent resources available online, and I suggest checking out [i]TrueAchievements[/i] for helpful tips.

Aside from that one multiplayer achievement, the others are relatively easy to obtain. However, keep in mind that the majority of the achievements in this game are centred around online and multiplayer play.

After the last time I played this game, quite a bit of time passed. I went from Xbox to PC and have been wanting to get this game again for all this time. The game is beautiful. Mechanics are great as always. However, there is one thing that absolutely ruins the game for me and that thing is the abundance of hackers; I spent most of my time setting up my classes and vehicles, only to go into a public match right afterwards. I am not exaggerating when I say this match was getting bent over and f--ked from behind. Hackers in the enemy team, killing everyone from places that you would never hit in vanilla BFV. It instantly turned me off from the game and I have already submitted a refund request.

Despite the fact that I have enjoyed playing this game, it is terribly unbalanced and design aspects of it seem to be so poorly thought through I would be incapable of giving a good review before these issues are resolved. 

Before I list the issues I have with this game, I would first like to acknowledge the positive aspects of it;

It still plays like a battlefield game, and is good if you'd just like a battlefield game in ww2, though you may want to instead go play BF 1942.

The game offers a lot of customization for characters, weapons, and vehicle skins that make these things unique. 

The assignments, weekly challenges, and daily assignments encourage players to try different playstyles and show off difficult achievements through their rewards. 

Now for the issues I have with this game: 

Firstly, the Anti-cheat: It's not uncommon to join a match and have at least one enemy using an aimbot to get unrealistic or impossible kills, reporting them may eventually get them banned, but it does nothing for the immediate match or matches. This is unacceptable since easy anti-cheat is easy to implement, and previous titles like BF 4 do not have this issue as rampantly. 

Weapon and vehicle balancing: German Tiger 1s, greyhounds, p51 mustangs, Stg 1-5 and sturmgewehr assault rifles, all are almost completely superior to the counterparts from other nationalities. The only explanation for this seems to be due to historical exaggeration and their importance in pop culture. On the opposite side, the Type-97 both tank and LMG, BAR m1918A2, M1941 Johnson, all perform worse than almost every other weapon or vehicle and have near no reason to pick them. 

Classes: The Assault has access to the best rifles for close and mid-range engagements, making them the most effective anti-personnel class, but are also the designated anti-tank and are able to carry the most anti-tank equipment, also making them the best for destroying enemy vehicles. This encourages players, especially solo players, to ritualistically select the assault class over all others. This is so rampant that 9/10 times the top squad will be mostly if not all assault classes at the end of a match. On the opposite end of the spectrum, the recon class is almost entirely useless as a team support class. Spotting does not last long enough to be viable, and sniping enemies from long distances does very little to enemy performance since medics can quickly get teamates up and easily evade most sniper fire. Spawn beacons also are not effective for changing the tides of war, as only squadmates can spawn on it, unless an ally pathfinder and their squad does, which rarely happens. 

The maps: It's not uncommon to spawn into a map where the starting location is an open field, with clear view from enemy tank or artillery fire, and almost immediately susceptible to enemy bombers at the start of the match. The game offers no AI anti-air to prevent spawn camping, and it happens frequently. This issue seems to be a byproduct of a deeper issue with the maps being simply too small, enemy planes frequently fly over other team HQs to maneuver, and there is very little space between objectives. 

Eurocentrism: The game falls into the stereotypical and ahistorical US and Britain vs Germany perception of WW2. It refuses to acknowledge the eastern front in it's entirety, with no soviet weapons, vehicles, skins, or campaign stories. While there is a french campaign telling a little known story about the french Senegalese Tirailleurs, there is little representation of french weapons, or vehicles in game, and even less cosmetics for the previously mentioned Senegalese Tirailleurs. There is also no mention of any conflicts in Asia outside the US vs Japanese pacific front, including the Chinese civil war, Japanese invasion of mainland China, or the soviet conflicts with the Japanese. Other lesser known conflicts are also still ignored, such as the Spanish civil war, absolutely no content including Italy, Italian invasion of Ethiopia, German invasion of Poland, Territorial conflicts for Czechoslovakia, or the Mexican Reform War. the most disappointing aspect of these facts, is that despite the wealth of possibilities for interesting maps, weapons, conflicts, and stories the game could tell in a WW2 setting, it instead decides to tell the same exhausted story and engage with the same conflicts that any other WW2 game has already told. 


So, after my big gripes with this game, how could these issues be fixed? Well, many of these glaring problems are foundational, and would require complete reworking of core mechanics, as well as entirely new story content for a game that is no longer getting DLC. But here's ways I think would help or fix these issues:

Implement easy anti-cheat for automatically banning users who use clients for aimbotting and other cheats. If not this, at least allow users to block other players they don't want to be in a match with, to prevent them from joining matches with blacklisted players. 

Nerf the accuracy and damage of many of the over powered assault rifles, allow tanks to be damaged by incendiary grenades thrown into their engine block's air intake panel, slow turret rotation on many tanks to their more realistic speeds, prevent tank turret rotation when the engine is disabled. For the Tiger 1 specifically, increase damage taken substantially when directly hit in the engine block from behind, Buff the Japanese type-97 tank to be faster, and capable of out-Maneuvering the now slowed tank turret rotation for most tanks. Increase type-97 shell capacity. 

For LMGs, the guns should be completely reworked, with all LMGs operating like MMGs currently do (only fired from hip without bipod), and MMGs not equippable in hand when on the move, and must be set up on a static position with a few seconds set up time. In return, the damage, fire rate, and accuracy from bipod (or tripod for MMGs) of all LMGs and MMGs should be significantly buffed, with MMGs doing similar damage as sniper rifles, and allowing for one shot kills to the head at full enemy health. Low capacity LMGs such as the BAR should also have buffed hip-fire accuracy to better represent their original role as trench-clearing guns. 

The Anti-vehicle aspects of Assault should be separated out into it's own designated class, with primary weapons similar to medic, but offering it's own sub-class for anti-air or anti-tank. Anti-air could have it's own unique target guide for the speed and trajectory of enemy aircraft, similar to the target in Warthunder. While Anti-tank could have buffs to panzerfaust, Bazooka, and piat ammo capacity, and damage to tanks and personnel carriers. The assault could instead offer a higher selection of anti-personnel traps and other devices to kill groups of enemy troops. 

As for the maps and the eurocentric settings, the game would need to be completely reworked with more story content and larger maps in order to appropriately alleviate these problems. 

If you've read this far, thank you for reading my review, I would like to reiterate that I have enjoyed the game, and my criticism come from a feeling of missed potential rather than hate or malice. I'd hope to see some or all of these issues changed, but for a game that is no longer getting content it is not expected. Have fun and have a nice day!

[h1] Absolute Disaster [/h1]
Battlefield V… a game rife with controversy pre-launch and post-launch, abandoned just as it started to truly improve.

Battlefield V on the other hand, the game following Battlefield 1 (yes, this series has awful naming), is set during World War II and instead of feeling like a passion project with a team that’s dedicated on giving us a somewhat immersive war experience with the Frostbite engine, DICE instead opted to try their own spin on WWII… a bad one.

Let’s start with…

[h1] The Disastrous Pre-Release [/h1]
Battlefield 1 was generally well received, but the community had it’s complaints, especially after coming from Battlefield 4. Going back in time and limiting the sandbox wasn’t what a lot of people wanted, but still, the game was massively praised for it’s graphics, sound effects and it’s ability to immerse players in WWI on modern systems. A lot of players also did really enjoy it once they got used to the gameplay and updates increased the content in the game.

Before the release of BFV, there was tons of speculation about what era the next game would be set in. Eventually it was announced the title of the game would be Battlefield V and would be set during WWII.

Players were excited, WWII involves possibly the most famous battles in the history of the human race. This was DICE’s opportunity to show these battles in a first-person shooter on one of the most graphically impressive game engines out there.

When the trailer dropped… all hopes were shattered. Characters were running around with prosthetic limbs firing machine guns during WWII, characters said cheesy lines despite the fact that they were currently in the middle of combat, they wore ridiculous outfits that real soldiers never wore and overall the historical accuracy was basically non-existent.

It felt like a parody of World War II. They took WWII as a setting and then just tossed the worst of modern game art into it, hoping to score some easy monetization.

There was also backlash due to game allowing you to pick your characters gender and race, despite it not being historically accurate for certain genders or race to fight on certain sides. Personally, it’s not something I care much about, especially in multiplayer, but I can see arguments from both sides being somewhat valid.

DICE decided to mock fans at the launch party for the game. At the party, a big screen, with messages handpicked by DICE, containing a mix of nonsense “feedback” and actual valid reactions from members of the community.

Nonsense such as “Genderfield 5” and actual valid community reactions such as “What the f*** was the developers thinking!”

Instead of listening to actual feedback and communicating properly with people, they decided to ignore everyone and openly mock the community, regardless of whether the feedback was good or not.

Great start… let’s move onto the actual game.

[h1] The Campaign [/h1]
The campaign is in the same format as BF1, “War Stories” which have the player playing through different soldiers stories throughout the war.

Like BF1, the game starts off with a fairly strong prologue war story. This war story brings us through each year of the war from a different soldiers perspective.

While BF1’s prologue intends to show you the absolute horrors of WWI and the loss of life which occurred, BFV’s is more about the epic scale of WWII, as you go from several different fronts on land and in the sky.

It's definitely not bad, the music is great and it really gets you excited to see how DICE have brought WWII to such a graphically impressive engine.

After that, it all goes wrong… while the war stories in BF1’s war stories weren’t amazing, some of them had their moments and the levels themselves were well put together. The worst thing about BF1’s campaign was how it didn’t feel as big as it should’ve.

BFV takes this to another level while also being worse at absolutely everything else. You thought you’d see D-Day on the Frostbite engine? Think again.

I wouldn’t recommend the campaign at all. It takes the worst from BF1 and amplifies it massively.

[h1] The Multiplayer [/h1]
The multiplayer for BFV was often panned for its historical inaccuracies, however I don’t really care about that, I care about the gameplay.

They made some significant changes in the multiplayer for BFV, some good, some bad.

The movement is possibly my favourite change to BFV. It’s fast and very fluid. Sliding works very well and you have a lot of control over your character while doing it, it allows good players to out-manoeuvre those who haven’t mastered the movement as well. This game also introduced sprinting while crouched, a very nice addition which allows you to keep a lower profile while keeping some speed.

Characters now naturally goes onto their back when prone in certain positions, rather than always lying on their stomach. You also have control over how your character lands when falling from smaller heights, you can roll which takes longer but negates all damage, or you can just fall and take the damage, but you’ll be a bit quicker to get your sights up. It’s a very nice system.

They removed spotting, which has been in the series since at least the original Bad Company. Instead of spotting, you can now ping locations similar to say Valorant.

You can still get traditionally spotted if enemies are using certain combat roles, but later on they added a “You are spotted” indicator to let you know that you’re currently marked for the entire enemy team, a great addition.

Speaking of combat roles, they added these on top of the traditional class system. Each class has different combat roles, which basically just changes the perks you have. It's stupidly convoluted and overcomplicates things unnecessarily. They had planned to add additional combat roles post-launch, but didn’t bother because of the games poor reception.

The UI in general is dreadful. For example, there’s some fun challenges to unlock skins for weapons, however you need to ACTIVATE each challenge for each weapon individually in the main menu. You can only have 4 active at a time, if you complete them, you then have to LEAVE whatever server you’re in, activate more and then look for another server. This is an absolute nightmare if you’re playing with friends. Games like CoD4 came out in 2007 and you could complete any challenge at any time without ever leaving the game.

Maps in multiplayer aren’t great either, a lot of the maps are too big even for 64 player conquest. You basically have to play as a medic in this game in order to do any effective push as there’s often not enough cover and medics are the only class with effective smokes. If you don’t have several medics who creates smokes for your team, you aren’t going to advance at all. It feels very unbalanced, especially in the linear game modes.

The new fortification system is a great addition to BF, which allows players to build fortifications all over maps.

It’s not overly complicated too like say Fortnite. You simply take out your fortification tool and outlines of what and where you can build will appear around you, simply go up to them, hold left click and bam, you just built something.

This was a great addition that I was originally reluctant about, but it did grow on me.

[h1] Overall Thoughts [/h1]
The campaign really isn’t worth playing, the multiplayer had some good changes but it’s definitely more frustrating than BF1 and just when DICE started to make some excellent progress, they abandoned the game to create the terrible Battlefield 2042.

A terrible pre-release, a terrible release and a terrible post-release filled with tons of broken promises and poor communication.

As of 2023, buy Battlefield 1 instead.

Let's get it started. Multiplayer review only.
The review has been significantly updated as I've played over 1000 hours.

✅Incredibly beautiful. The game looks excellent, the visual artists' attention to detail has always been at a high level.
✅Shooting. Pleasing and instantly understandable. The most ridiculous and annoying suppression mechanics has finally been and completely REMOVED, which is 100% right decision, IMHO. However, the random element in the automatic gun behavior makes the shooting overly casual and skillless.
✅Connection. There is a great netcode that feels amazing. Shot hit registration works admirably, sometimes there are problems, but rarely (at low ping).
✅Collision meshes & hitboxes. 10/10, not joking. Previous BF games feel WAY worse in comparison. So, Shooting + Connection + Collision meshes = the smoothest shooter experience I’ve ever had (especially with 165+ FPS).
✅No 3D spot. The absence of an actual wallhack when spotting, as in BF4/1 is fantastic, IMHO.
✅Breakthrough. An exceptionally fun meat-grinder gamemode.
✅Optimization. Excellent optimization and many settings to achieve individual FPS/Visual results. The FPS limit can be set according to the desired value or according to the frequency of your monitor without V-sync. If you are interested in maximizing FPS, set everything to minimum except the mesh, which should be set to ultra (enemy's visibility).
✅HUD settings. It's just as customizable as in BF4/1. Flexible & convenient.
✅Discount. At almost all sales you can buy the game up to -95%.
✅Cheaters. The game used to be notorious for having a lot of cheaters, but to give the devil his due - after the clunky anticheat update, it's no longer an issue.
✅Aggressive Sniping. Objectively the hardest-to-play and purely skill-based playstyle in the game, but very enjoyable. This is the only reason for me to play this game and the only reason why I'm almost the last aggressive sniper that's left over here. Let ZK players try it out and they will cry like babies from the difficulty.
⚠️Squad. Playing in a squad with friends is just as damn fun and highly effective as playing with random people in your squad is boring and unproductive.
⚠️Minor new mechanics and reworked old mechanics. First aid kits, ammo, supply boxes, the ability to revive a squad member, and rewards for squad points are fun but kill the squad dependence and are imbalanced to the extend where farmers dominate even more.
⚠️Classes. The mechanics are fine and the perks are now immediately available. Yet, there's one perk in the game that ruins the balance entirely (see the details below).
❌Team Balance. I don't know what they were smoking when they decided to remove the ability to switch teams. There's literally no auto-balance, and if you want to fix the game's boolshit, be ready to perform stupid shenanigans like leaving the server and rejoining several times until it finally places you on the team you want. At the beginning of a new match, all player positions are the same regardless of the results of the previous map. Of course, the overall composition changes a little, because some players leave, but in 90% of cases this does not affect the balance at all and one team is totally dominated by the other for several maps in a row. The biggest cons and degeneracy I've ever seen.
❌Weapon balance. Unfortunately, traditionally for BF everything is not just bad, everything is catastrophic and terrible bad. Obviously OP guns with incredible high rate of fire or versatility + easy control (M2 Carbine, Type 2A, ZK-383 etc.), shotguns (several one-shots per sec.), DMR, Sniper DMR (ZH-29, etc.) completely eliminate the balance.
❌Class balance. There is simply no point in you choosing any other class than medic if you [strike]are a low-skilled degenerate[/strike] want to win every shootout and survive as long as possible (read below for detailed explanation).
❌Servers. Convenient custom server tools are missing, as they'd solve most of the game's issues. Unlike BF1/4, there are simply no servers where OP weapons are banned or kicked and the team balance is maintained. Pairing it with the above mentioned downsides you now clearly see why the game is a huge failure.
❌Maps. As I said earlier, appearance is amazing. But there are few of them and many of them are unbalanced and boring.

Low on content and rough around the edges, Battlefield V feels like it was butchered for the sake of future "free" updates. What's here is fun, but it isn't a full-fledged experience, and it feels like an investment in an incomplete game. Oh, and did I mention all the cheaters running around? Sad.

Well, is it better than Battlefield 1? No. Is it still a good battlefield experience? Yes. Since it's based on WW2, we get access to more advanced weapons, attachments (you get the Nydar reflex sight for assault rifles), gadgets and vehicles so if you're interested in having a more advanced loadout then it will suit your needs.

The singleplayer campaign is decent but nothing spectacular like the one we experience in Battlefield 1. The stories told are great but the missions themselves don't really feel that good tbh. I only liked The Last Tiger chapter, which is really good overall and finally gave us an experience from the German perspective. All other chapters are pretty average gameplay wise. 

Multiplayer is pretty enjoyable, yes maybe not at as good as Battlefield 1, but still very solid in its own way. You can slide, crouch run, lean while aiming, fortify the area, call-in squad reinforcements if you're the squad leader - all of which you couldn't do in Battlefield 1, so mechanically it is definitely better. The maps are mostly good as well, on full servers the matches gets chaotic and intense in good old battlefield fashion. The only way to play multiplayer matches right now is through server browsers and using appropriate filters to suit your needs. You can easily get many EU and Asian servers with near to full player counts even at off peak hours.

Music deserves a huge shoutout! Soundtrack in Battlefield V, infused with WW2 flavor, hits all the right notes. During multiplayer matches, the theme kicks in at intense points and elevates the whole feel and experience of the game. BFV features some of the best variants of the classic battlefield theme! (The remastered Battlefield 1942 theme and Wake Island OST are bloody amazing)

One thing I didn't like at all is the fact that it's slightly a visual downgrade from Battlefield 1. I don't know what but something's off about the way it looks, maybe it's the filters or post processing, but it definitely doesn't deliver a clean image. Atmospherically also, it's somewhat a downgrade from Battlefield 1.

I understand why some people might be a little disappointed by this game specially after playing Battlefield 1, because in some areas it definitely feels like a slight downgrade instead of an upgrade. But then, Battlefield 1 was DICE's 'lightning in a bottle' moment, so following up to that was always going to be really really hard. I do like the new stuff they introduced in this game like crouch running, leaning, squad reinforcement calls, fortifications etc but it definitely had a lot more potential which could have made it a much more solid experience. Still, it's a pretty good game in the battlefield series so i recommend picking this up.

I'm rewriting my review since there's a plume of brain dead fan boys responding to it... 

I played this game for half an hour. Didn't play single player beyond the basic tutorial they make you play through, since BF has always been a game I purchase for MP.

I was excited to play this game. I wanted it to be good. I load up my first match and it's some underground subway map, which I've since found out that a lot of people like because it's a good opportunity to grind unlocks. I picked my traditional medic loadout and spawned in on a squadmate. A few minutes into the match I'm getting demolished. I'd get a few kills going and think I'm about to make a comeback only to get lasered as soon as I even peak a corner. Someone then mentions in the chat that someone is hacking and I look and sure enough the enemy top fragger has 90+ kills with 2 deaths; blatantly cheating. Now this is where some of the people upset with my review took issue saying that I was only assuming he's cheating and that good players can easily have high KDs because they utilize vehicles. This map is infantry only. There's no planes, no tanks... Is it possible? Sure, it's possible. But after sitting through the rest of that game and getting killed by him a few times throughout the remainder of it, I was certain he was cheating. 

Another player mentioned in chat there is no anti-cheat for BFV. I was stunned to hear that a triple A game could actually have an online MP that has no anti-cheat so I did some googling for myself and sure enough BFV launched without an anti-cheat and they claim to use a mixture of detection methods to detect cheaters. Well, in my very brief experience with the game it's not working at all. There are VERY few games that I see blatant cheaters in because for the most part detection methods against things like aimbots are effective in 2020. In fact, I've played plenty of games where I've never encountered someone I could say for certain was cheating at all. BFV isn't one of them.

And for people saying "Well it's a PC game of course there's going to be cheaters". That's no excuse to have such a lackluster approach to cheating. This is a huge reason why people who've been playing PC for years and years miss the days of server lists where server admins could easily weed out cheaters from their community and people playing legitimately could enjoy a generally cheat-free environment. 

The next gripe I had with this game was the goofy cosmetics of the game to which some people replied "If you want authenticity go play x, y, z game"  or "List of games without pacific front/Stalingrad". To the first point of go play another game... I don't want a simulator. I want a curated experience that has artwork that's authentic to the time period. Call of Duty World at War did a better job at that than this game.

To the second point of games without the pacific and/or Stalingrad... The list is very short, and they're primarily MP only OR games that focus solely on the American involvement in the war (ex: Medal of Honor or 1942 Pacific Front). 

To close out my review I want to address people who say there ARE pacific maps in BFV and I want to redact parts of my original review saying there wasn't. I've been corrected in that there ARE pacific maps. I never got to play them, and I'd seen reviews stating there was no pacific theatre info at all.

It's definitely a cool thing to have seen Norway and N. Africa campaigns in the game but what the hell were they thinking making such a mockery with the cosmetics? All you have to do is watch the reveal trailer and see some lady holding with a literal hook for a hand holding a thompson fighting in a house. That's completely overlooking the totally out of place braveheart face paint they have on in the campaign. BF 1942, BF2, BF1943, and BFBC1 & 2 are some of the greatest games of the 2000s and that reputation and nostalgia is what made me want to give this game a chance. Unfortunately it isn't even close to living up and has ruined any chance I'll ever spend money on a BF game in the near future.

Also lets mention the thompson. An American gun in the game, yet for some reason the game launched with no playable American faction even in multiplayer. Small detail, but it's just another example of how ridiculously they butchered any semblance of historical authenticity this game could have had.

To everyone saying I didn't give this game a chance because I played only 30 minutes of it, I say this. I gave it the same chance I'd give any other multiplayer game. If any other game I had ever played had so many glaring issues in 30 minutes of gameplay and an hour of google  searching and videos, I'd skip it and get a refund on it too. To those of you saying I have too high of expectations, yes... I do have high expectations from a company that makes billions of dollars a year to produce decent products for consumers. Why do they make billions of dollars a year? Because they're a company that's known to have produced excellent Battlefield games in the past. The game might be fun for some, but for those of you looking for a WW2 game with an authentic feeling environment etc. look elsewhere. The only reason I'd recommend this game is if you don't care about that and are the kind of person to excuse an absolutely neglectful approach to weeding out cheaters. Even then, be warned that EA and DICE have said that they may be scrapping the updates to this game in the near future so the support may be coming to an end very soon.

Feel free to continue "educating" me about how this game is actually flawless though in the replies, I'm enjoying reading them.
